change.describe: branch `pr-67876-flat` of sentry-67876-flat against f3b740199ef0b8057c2c68a377fd3b4d42346deb (merge-base f3b7401)
change.title: pr-67876-flat
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: OAuth `state` is a constant, not a per-flow secret, so it gives no CSRF protection
findings.body:
`state = pipeline.signature`, and `Pipeline.signature` is `md5(<view class names>)` (src/sentry/pipeline/base.py:132-133). It is the same value for every user and every request, and anyone can compute it. The test hardcodes it (`9cae5e88...`). The check at line 412 only confirms the caller knows that constant. It does not bind the callback to the browser session that started the flow.

An attacker can install the GitHub app on their own account, authorize it, and get a valid `code`. They can then lure an org admin to `/extensions/github/setup/?code=<attacker code>&state=<constant>`. The victim's pipeline records `github_authenticated_user` as the attacker, and the org can end up linked to the attacker-controlled installation. Use a random, per-flow nonce. Store it with `pipeline.bind_state` and compare it with `constant_time_compare`. Do not reuse the signature.

findings.title: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError for integrations that have no stored sender
findings.body:
`sender` is only stored in `build_integration` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy (line 376). The only caller I found that passes it is the webhook `created` handler (src/sentry/integrations/github/webhook.py:201-209). Integrations created by other paths have no `sender` key. That includes integrations that predate this field and integrations created from the pipeline, where state has no `sender`.

For such an integration that still has no OrganizationIntegration, this line raises KeyError and the user gets a 500. Use `.get` chains. Decide explicitly what to do when the sender is unknown: fail closed with `error(...)`, or fall back to the old behavior. Add a test for it.

findings.title: Network and HTTP errors from the token exchange and user lookup are not handled
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` at line 423 sits outside the `try`. `get_user_info` at line 434 calls `raise_for_status()` (src/sentry/identity/github/provider.py:16). A timeout or a non-2xx response from GitHub, for example a revoked token, becomes an unhandled exception and a 500. The sibling `OAuth2CallbackView.exchange_token` returns an error payload in the same situation. Wrap both calls and return `error(...)`.

findings.title: redirect_uri and state are interpolated into the authorize URL without encoding
findings.body: `redirect_uri` is a full URL placed into the query string unencoded. Use `urlencode`. The new test also asserts the unencoded form (test_integration.py:235), so it would need updating.

findings.title: `test_installation_not_found` no longer tests the 404 installation path
findings.body: The test stubs a 404 on `/app/installations/...` and used to assert "The GitHub installation could not be found." Now the callback is sent with `state=ddd023d8...`, which does not match the pipeline signature. The pipeline returns the generic error from the state check in `OAuthLoginView` (integration.py:412-413), and the test asserts "Invalid installation request." The `IntegrationError` 404 branch in `build_integration` is no longer exercised. The test now covers a bad state, not a missing installation. Send the valid state so the pipeline reaches `build_integration`, and keep the original assertion. Add a separate test for the bad-state case.

findings.title: No test for a mismatched OAuth state with a valid code, or for an installation with no stored sender
findings.body: The new `OAuthLoginView` branches are only covered by the happy path and by the user-mismatch test. The missing cases are a wrong `state`, a token exchange that returns no `access_token`, a `/user` response with no `login`, and an existing Integration whose metadata has no `sender` (see the KeyError finding).

contracts.action: New OAuthLoginView step: redirect to GitHub authorize, then on callback exchange the code for a token and fetch the GitHub user login
contracts.equivalent_path: OAuth2LoginView/OAuth2CallbackView in src/sentry/identity/oauth2.py, which uses a random per-flow state and handles exchange errors
contracts.before_after: The existing path generates a random state stored in pipeline state, verifies it on callback, and returns an error payload when the token exchange fails. The new path uses the static pipeline signature as state and has no handling for exchange or user-lookup exceptions.
contracts.visible_effect: Users hit a GitHub authorize redirect first. A failed check renders github-integration-failed.html with a postMessage to the opener.
contracts.failure_mode: A predictable state allows login CSRF. An exception from safe_urlopen or get_user_info gives a 500.

contracts.action: Compare the authenticated GitHub user with integration.metadata['sender']['login'] when the Integration exists without an OrganizationIntegration
contracts.equivalent_path: Webhook installation `created` handler, which is the only writer of `sender`
contracts.before_after: The webhook stores sender id and login only for `created` events. The new check assumes the key always exists.
contracts.visible_effect: On mismatch the user gets a generic invalid-request dialog.
contracts.failure_mode: KeyError and a 500 when `sender` is absent.

contracts.action: Inline the FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR check in the pipeline advancer
contracts.before_after: Same behavior; `provider_id == 'github'` replaces membership in the one-element list.

summary: The change adds a GitHub OAuth login step and a check that the authenticated GitHub user is the installation's sender. There are two real defects in the integration code. The OAuth `state` is the static pipeline signature, so it gives no CSRF protection. The sender check does `metadata[\"sender\"][\"login\"]` and raises KeyError, which is a 500, for any integration with no stored sender. `test_installation_not_found` now exercises the bad-state path instead of the 404 installation path. There are also minor error-handling and URL-encoding gaps. The pipeline_advancer change is a harmless inlining.
